lawyer:
Rafi Ahmed, Advocate-------For the Petitioner. 
Chowdhury Morshed Kamal  Tipu, Advocate------For the Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
Sadaran Bima Corporation-------Petitioner
VS
Sylhet Pauroshava and others-------Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-12-1988 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 300 of 1989 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 28-12-1986 passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 117 of 1981 should not he set aside.

2. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 112 of 1981 to the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet impleading the petitioner as defendant No. 1 and opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 as defendant Nos.2 and 3 for declaration that order of defendant No.2 Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet dated 13-2-1981 disallowing tire release of the suit land to plaintiff Pourashava and directing to release of the property to defendant No. 1 Shadharon Bima Corporation is illegal, ultra vires, malicious and further for passing decree of permanent as well as mandatory injunction.

3. The case of the plaintiff-appellant, in brief is that the suit land originally belonged to Sylhet Pourashava which was acquired by it in LA case No.109/1901-1902. The Sylhet Pourshava Board was superseded by Government of Assam by Notification dated 10-2-39 for two years and the properties of Sylhet Municipal board were vested to the Crown and during this period of supersession the Governor of Assam granted lease of the suit land for 30 years to Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. by a registered Lease deed dated 18-9-1939. The Sylhet Industrial Bank constructed a two-storied building on the suit Land and carried their business. The said bank faced with financial difficulties and later by the order of Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Ford William in Bengal dated 25-6-47 it was amalgamated with M/s Mohaiakshmi Bank Ltd. M/s Mohaiakshmi bank Ltd. which held the assets of Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. and transferred the suit land along with building and other structures thereon to Arjya Insurance Co. by a registered Kabala deed dated 23-2-48. During Last S/S operation of 1956-57, the suit land was recorded in the name of Arjya Insurance Co. The suit land along with building and other structures were requisitioned in LA Case No. 42/B of 1950-51. Subsequently the suit land along with building and other structures were treated as enemy/vested property in VP Case No. 58/68-69. Plaintiff-appellant by its memo No.514 dated 22-3-1978 prayed to Deputy Commissioner Sylhet for release of the suit property in favour of Pourashava and Deputy Commissioner Sylhet by his memo No. DV/LG/3PS-12/(1)/78/909 dated 20-7-1978 directed the plaintiff-appellant to take steps for correction of record of right in the name of Sylhet Pourashava. Accordingly application was made for correction of record of right whereon, after due notices, orders were passed on 28-8-1978 for correcting the record of rights of the schedule land in the name of the plaintiff-appellant. But the property was not being released, so Pourashava moved the matter to Ministry of LA and LR whereupon the Ministry called for a report from Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet but no report has yet been submitted. Plaintiff-appellant Pourashava also, took up the matter for release of the property with Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) who in his reply to the Pourashava stated that record of rights were corrected in the name of the plaintiff-appellant and that the suit land being enemy/vested property by NP Case No. 58/68-69 and under requisition in the Requisition Case No. 42/B/50-51 and thus, he requested for necessary action in such content. On the other hand, the defendant respondent No. 1 Sadaran Birr a Corporation moved to the Ministry of Commerce and Ministry which advised the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Sylhet to look into the case. The defendant-respondent No.1 claimed title of the suit property and prayed for release of the property to them. Without reference to the earlier correspondence with Pourashava the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Sylhet observed that he had nothing to do with regard to the right and title in the land and advised the parties to take recourse to the competent Court of law but instructed the requisition authority by his order dated 13-2-1981 to pay rent to Arjya insurance Company which according to him stood amalgamated with defendant-respondent No.1, Sadaran Bima Corporation and directed de-requisition in favour of defendant No.1 which is illegal, ultra-vires, malicious and void and hence the suit.

4. The case of the defendant-respondent No. 1 Sadharon Bima Corporation, in brief, is that the suit land was vested to the Crown i.e, the then Government of India free from all encumbrances and when the suit land was in possession of the Government of Assam, it granted lease to Indus-trial Bank Ltd. by a registered bilateral lease deed dated 18-9-1939. The said Industrial Bank constructed permanent two-storied building on the suit land by taking permission from the then Sylhet Municipal Board by improving the condition of land at huge cost and paid rent to the Government and subsequently said Industrial Bank was amalgamated with the Mohalakkshmi Bank by the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature of Fort William of Bengal and on such amalgamation assets for the Industrial Bank vested on the Mohalakkshmi Bank, while Mohalakkshmi Bank is in possession of the suit land, the building and other structures thereon transferred the same to Arjya Insurance Co. Ltd. for consideration of Taka 40,000 by a registered deed dated 23-2-1948, whereupon the Arjya Insurance Co. became exclusive owner and named the said building as Arjya Insurance Building. During Last S/S operation, the suit land and building thereon was recorded in the name of Arjya Insurance Co. as statutory tenant under the Government and records of right had been finally printed and published in the name of Arjya Insurance Company without any objection either by the Sylhet Municipality or anybody else and it is maintained till date. The then Government of East Pakistan for Office accommodation requisitioned the said building from the possession of Arjya Insurance Co. Ltd. In RC Case No. 42/B of 1950-51 and paid monthly rent at the rate of Taka 200 per month to the said company admitting the title and possession of Arjya Insurance Company. In exercising Powers conferred by rule 181 of Defense of Pakistan rule by order dated 11-9-1965 the assets and liabilities of the Arjya Insurance company being unit of Life Insurance Co. of India was vested in Pakistan Insurance Corporation established under Pakistan Insurance Act, 1952 and since then all the assets and Liabilities of all units of the life Insurance Co. Ltd. of India falling within the territory of Pakistan vested in the Insurance Corporation and the said corporation settled many claim of Arjya Insurance Company up to 1971. In 1972 after liberation of Bangladesh the Pakistan Insurance Corporation was renamed as Bangladesh Insurance Corporation under PO No. 18/72 and all assests and liabilities of Pakistan Insurance Corporation falling within Bangladesh Territory vested in Bangladesh insurance Corporation and Subsequently the said corporation was dissolved and vested into Teesta Bima Corporation with all assests and liabilities by PO No. 161 of 1972. Then Sadharan Bima Corporation was constituted and all the assets of Teesta and Kamafully Bima corporation vested in the defendant-respondent No. 1 Sadaron Bima corporation which realizes monthly rents from then allottees of the suit property through the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet with the knowledge of the Pourashava and when the suit property was necessitated for their own use and enjoyment, the Sadaran Bima corporation applied for derequisition of the suit property and the collector is considering the necessity of the Sadaran Bima Corporation passed order on 13-2-1981 favouring derequisition of the suit property in favour of the Sadaran Bima Corporation and, as such, suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

5. The parties led evidence in support of their respective claims. After hearing the trial Court dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiff is not in possession of the suit land while the defendant No. 1 is in possession, who got rent of the suit premises and record of right has been prepared in defendant No. 1's name and without filing suit for recovery of khas possession instant suit is not maintainable; lease was not granted by the Sylhet Pourashava, rather Government of Assam granted lease to the predecessor of the petitioner the defendant No.1 constructed structures in the suit land and as per the provision of section 7 and 8 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act the plaintiff is not entitled to get possession.

6. The appellate Court reversed the finding of the trial Court and decreed suit contending that the Sylhet Municipality being 'local authority' it's interest cannot be vested upon the Government on the ground of lease. The appellate Court found that period of lease is 30 years being granted by Government of Assam during temporary supersession of Sylhet Municipality and, as such, after elapse of 30 years the suit properties reverted back to the Sylhet Municipality, so laying claim by the defendants in the suit land is illegal, arbitrary and is of no legal effect. The appellate Court further found that the suit property cannot be termed as enemy property as the property is leasehold property having granted by Government of Assam for 30 years during temporary supersession of the municipality. The appellate Court further held that the lessee can remove structures being built in the suit land after de-requisition of the suit property and, as such, there will be no obstruction and hindrance is getting the suit property by the plaintiff without laying claim in the structures standing in the suit land. The appellate Court held that the plaintiff may take recourse for de-requisition of the suit land before any competent authority and after the purpose of requisition being over the government may take step for de-requisition of the suit land in favour of real owner.

7. Mr Rafi Ahmed learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the suit is clearly had for the defect of parties but the appellate Court without adverting the vital aspects found the suit is maintainable which caused failure of justice. He next submits that the suit property has been leased out by the government of Assam to Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd by lease-deed dated 18-9-1939 where structures have been built by the said bank and subsequently the property is transferred to Arjyo Insurance Company by a deed of sale dated 23-2-1948 and, as such, the suit as framed is not maintainable but the appellate Court erroneously decreed the suit. Learned advocate further averred that as per the provision of defense of Pakistan Ordinance, rules, PO 18/72 and 161/72 right, title and interest of Arjyo Insurance Company has been devolved upon the defendant No. I and, as such, the plaintiffs claim over the suit land is not sustainable.

8. On the other hand, Mr Chaudhury Morshed Kamal, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 submits that in lease deed date 18-9-1939 exhibit-1, it was stipulated that after expiry of the period of lease that is for 30 years, the lease shall not be renewed as of right and the lower appellate Court rightly held that the period of lease has been ceased by expiry of time. He next submits that in the subsequent sale deed dated 23-2-1948, exhibit-3 entered into between Mahaiaxmi Bank with Arjya Insurance Company Ltd duration of the original lease has been mentioned for 30 years and, as such, the defendant No.1 cannot claim title to the suit property. He next submits that admittedly the suit property has been acquired for Sylhet Paurashva and during its supersession for two years Assam Government leased out the said property to Sylhet industrial Bank and, as such, after expiry of the lease period, naturally the property reverted back' to the plaintiff and as the government requisitioned the said land for government purposes and, as such, after de-requisition, the plaintiff is entitled to get back the property. He next submits that the defendant No.1 cannot Claim the property by virtue of wrong record of right and, as such, the appellate Court upon consideration of legal aspect as well as facts and circumstances rightly decreed the suit.

9. Having gone through the pleadings, impugned judgment and exhibits it appears that Sylhet Paurashava was owner of the suit land and being its temporary supersession Government of Assam leased out the said property by lease deed dated 18-9-1939 to Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd for 30 years, and after expiry of the lease period the tenure cannot be extended unless the lessee renewed it by any covenant. It is clear that there is no renewal of lease and, as such, Sylhet Paurashova remained owner of the suit property. Although lease deed has been executed by Assam Government for temporary supersession of Sylhet paurashova being for two years, but after elapse of that period Sylhet paurashova seized of its normal functions and naturally remained owner of the property in question.

10. In the instant case, the positive case of the plaintiff is that the suit property is acquired land of Sylhet Pourashava which has been acquired vide LA case No. 109/1901-1902 and admittedly due to supersession of Sylhet Municipality the government of Assam leased out the suit land to Sylhet Industrial Bank for 30 years on 18-9-1939 and the said bank in amalgamated with Mohalaxmi Bank and the said Mohalaxmi Bank transferred the suit land in favour of Arjyo Insurance Company by deed dated 23-2-1948 for the reminder period of earlier lease. So it is clear that the government of Assam leased out the suit land for 30 years mentioning the ownership of Sylhet municipality and, as such, after elapse of two years Sylhet Municipality resumed its function as before with full ownership of the suit land along with other properties and, as such, the trial Court's finding as vesting of title to defendant No.1 by, successive transfer is not at all tenable. Besides, after expiry of lease period no fresh lease has been granted to the predecessor of defendant No.1 or earlier lessee and it is also clear that 30 years lease of non-agricultural land is not a lease of perpetually. The said view is clearly established by a decision reported in 17 DLR 329.

Which is quoted below:

"Admittedly the suit-land is a Non-Agricultural land and it is also admitted that the defendant-appellants had obtained the lease of the suit land from plaintiffs predecessor in title. The only question to be examined is, whether the suit-land had vested in the Government. If the aforesaid lease is not a lease in perpetuity, the plaintiff is not a "rent-receiver" and, the suit-land has not vested in Government. It is evident from the terms of the lease as stated above, that it is a lease for a fixed term and not a lease in perpetuity. A lease in perpetuity is unknown to English law. In the country a lease in perpetuity can he created by ah express grant to that effect or by a necessary presumption raised by the terms of a grant and by an unambiguous and long possession. In this particular case there can be no manner' of doubt that the lease was for a fixed period and not a lease in perpetuity within the meaning of the Transfer of Property Act. Plaintiff was not, therefore, a "rent-receiver" in respect of the suit land."

11. The contention of the trial Court that Sylhet industrial bank took lease of the suit property from Assam Government and, as such, Sylhet municipality has no ownership therein which is not all correct because in the deed in question Government of Assam clearly mentioned that due to temporary supersession of Sylhet municipality, the lease deed has been executed by Government of Assam and, as such, finding of the trial Court is not all sustainable.

12. The trial Court also wrongly held that as the predecessor of defendant No.1 constructed pacca structure in the suit land, the plaintiff is not entitled to get possession as per section 2(5), 7 and 8 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act 1949. Such view is also not sustainable as because Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act 1949 expressly excludes any land vested in or in the possession of any local authority as per section 85A of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. In 39 DLR (AD) 16 it is held as under-

"The Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 expressly excludes any land vested "in or in the possession of any local authority". See section 85A clause (3). Therefore, the defendants could not take resort even to the provision of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. The reason in simple, because the application of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act would saddle the Municipality with certain legal obligations and, as such, the legislature expressly omitted the operation of such act insofar as any land vested in or in the possession of any local authority. So that the advantage which it gives and the dis-advantages which it imposes may not come into operation with regard to such land".

<u>13. The trial Court also committed error in holding that the suit is bad for defect of parties for non- impleading the vested property authority as defendant but the said view is an wrong approach as because the suit land is not vested property but even then Additional Deputy Commissioner has been impleaded as defendant No.2 'who looks after the vested property on behalf of the government and, as such, the findings of the trial Court is quite irrelevant. Besides no suit can fail merely for non-joinder or misjoinder of parties as per order 1 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In 49 DLR (AD) 151 it is held that "no suit can fail by reason merely of non-joinder of parties Order I Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure makes this legal position clear". Apart from this, the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff being not in possession of the suit land his suit is not maintainable without making prayer of khas possession is also not maintainable, since the property is in the possession of the Government, the plaintiffs suit is maintainable without making prayer for recovery of khas possession. In 43 DLR 109 it is held that—</u>

<u>"Hence the Government is holding the property treating the same to be of the plaintiff. If it is declared by the Court that it is not an abandoned property the Government will have no reason to possess the same and will be under obligation to restore possession to the plaintiff and no prayer for recovery of possession as a consequential relief is necessary. Hence the suit is quite maintain-able and it is not barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act."</u>

<u>14. Since the property is presently being used as requisition property, it can be de-requisitioned in favour of the rightful owner after ceasing its necessity.</u>

<u>15. Apart from this if anybody has no title in any property mere record of right will not confer title to him. The trial Court fails to consider the legal provisions and erroneously dismissed the suit.</u>

<u>16. The appellate Court on appreciation, of evidence both oral and documentary and also by proper interpretation of documents rightly reversed the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit with appreciable reasons and it is settled position of law that if the lower appellate Court reverse any judgment of the trial Court on proper assessment of the evidence on record, it calls for no interference under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.</u>

17. In the above circumstances I find no merit in the Rule and accordingly the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court Record be sent to the concern Court.

End.
